# ADR-0009: Feed retrieval never triggers acquisition; responses carry coverage

## Status

Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).

## Decision

Every Feed read (search, deref) is a pure read: it never scans, fetches, or blocks on a Provider. This deliberately deviates from Vendor's fetch-on-demand default (vendor ADR-0004) because Feed acquisition is browser-driven, minutes-slow, login-stateful, and quota-bound, none of which belongs inside a query path. Scans stay scheduled; the only demand-driven acquisition is the repair queue and the manual refresh command (ADR-0005). Because "no results" is ambiguous in a pull-based corpus, every search response carries coverage metadata (which Providers were scanned for the queried window, and when, from `source_scans`) so a consumer can distinguish "nothing published" from "not scanned yet" and request a scan out of band.

## Considered options

- Synchronous fetch-on-demand like Vendor: rejected, minutes-long latency and a logged-in browser dependency inside the retrieval path, with quota burn driven by query patterns instead of a schedule.
- Async scan-request queue: deferred until a real consumer proves the need.

Status: done.

Implements ADR-0009's coverage half. `src/coverage.ts` (new): `resolveCoverage(db, from, to)` enumerates
every window date via `dateRange` (`src/cli/config.ts`, previously unused, now wired in), reads all
`source_scans` rows in `[from, to]` in one query (new `ArticleDb.getSourceScanDates(from, to)` in `src/db.ts`),
and returns one `{ provider, scanned, gaps }` entry per entry in `PROVIDER_NAMES` (`src/providers/index.ts`,
the acquisition registry, 9 providers). A date counts as `scanned` if a `source_scans` row exists for that
provider/date regardless of status (a `failed`/`partial` scan still means the provider was attempted, which
is what ADR-0009 needs); everything else is a `gap`, meaning not-scanned-yet, not "nothing published".
Confirmed live that `source_scans.source` is always written from `cfg.name`/`name` (the provider's own
config name, `src/pipeline/extract.ts` lines 601/1748/2162), so keying strictly on `PROVIDER_NAMES` is
correct; the live `output/articles.db` also holds unrelated legacy rows under compound keys like
`wireone/economics` and unknown names like `breakingviews`/`columbia` from an older acquisition scheme,
which the resolver correctly ignores since it only looks up the 9 current provider keys.

`scripts/feedq.ts` `cmdSearch`: computes `coverage` once from `flags.from`/`flags.to` (both the article-mode
and `--in live-posts` JSON branches use the same window) via a new `resolveSearchCoverage` helper that opens
and closes its own read-only `ArticleDb`, matching the existing ope
